record.paper_title: Descriptions of Cantor Sets: A Set-Theoretic Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine whether one can obtain descriptive set-theoretic formulas for deterministic Cantor sets whose retained intervals have irrational end-points, while still allowing an iterated-function-system construction with K ≥ 2 components.

evidence.quote: The preceding survey has shown that three natural families of deterministic Cantor sets—two of measure zero with explicit descriptions and one of non–negative measure defined recursively—share a common symmetric architecture and possess rational construction end-points; indeed, the classical middle-third Cantor set lies in the intersection of all three.
(OP2) Irrational end-points. Find descriptive formulas when the retained intervals have irrational end-points, again allowing K ≥ 2 IFS components.

artifact.category_tag: Cantor sets and iterated function systems
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A deterministic Cantor set in [0,1] can be constructed by an iterated function system (IFS) consisting of K ≥ 2 contracting affine maps φ_i(x) = r_i x + a_i (i = 1, …, K) with disjoint images, so that the attractor C is the unique non-empty compact set satisfying C = ⋃_{i=1}^{K} φ_i(C). Equivalently, at each stage of the construction one specifies finitely many closed subintervals of [0,1] (the retained intervals) whose endpoints are determined by the maps φ_i; iterating the procedure yields a nested sequence of unions of intervals whose intersection is C.

For classical examples (such as the middle-thirds Cantor set and other symmetric, measure-zero or positive-measure variants in which all retained intervals have rational endpoints), one can give an explicit descriptive set-theoretic formula characterizing membership in C — for instance, by describing the digits of x in a suitable base expansion, yielding a Π^0_2 (or simpler arithmetical) defining condition.

Problem. Develop analogous descriptive set-theoretic formulas characterizing membership in deterministic Cantor sets C ⊆ [0,1] arising from IFS constructions with K ≥ 2 affine contractions in which at least some of the retained intervals have irrational endpoints. More precisely: exhibit, for as wide a class as possible of such IFS-generated Cantor sets with irrational construction endpoints, an explicit logical formula φ(x) (in the language of real arithmetic, or in terms of digit expansions in a chosen base, or in the projective/Borel hierarchy) such that x ∈ C ⇔ φ(x), and determine the descriptive complexity of the resulting class of sets. Alternatively, prove that no such uniform descriptive formulas can exist beyond the rational-endpoint case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem (OP2) in a 2025 survey on descriptions of Cantor sets, and no follow-up work providing such descriptive formulas for irrational-endpoint IFS Cantor sets was located. Status appears to remain open.
